Serie B: top 2 direct, 3rd-8th play off for the third place (3rd direct if 15+ points clear of 4th). Serie A: 18th-20th relegated directly, no play-out.

Serie C: one direct promotion per group (3) plus the national play-off winner (1). Serie B: 18th-20th direct plus 16th v 17th play-out (skipped if 17th is 5+ points behind 16th, then 17th goes down). The four relegated clubs are placed into Serie C groups A/B/C by geography with no quota; 2026-27 was A 0, B 3, C 1.
J2: top two automatic, 3rd-6th play off for the third place. J1: bottom three relegated, no J1/J2 play-off since 2024.
J3: top two automatic, 3rd-6th play off for the third place (J2 licence required). J2: bottom three relegated.

2026: Premier League bottom two relegated (Zhetysu, Kaisar); the First League's top two are promoted in a normal season. 2025 -> 2026 was a one-off 1 down / 3 up because the Premier League expanded from 14 to 16.

Virsliga 10th is relegated directly and 9th plays a two-legged play-off against the 2nd-placed Future League club for the last place; the Future League champion is promoted directly. One shared play-off place, so the real movement is between 1+1 and 2+2 each way.

I Lyga champion goes up, TOPLYGA 10th goes down directly; I Lyga 2nd meets TOPLYGA 9th over two legs for the second place, so only one of the two clubs in that tie plays in the top flight next season.

National Division: 15th and 16th down direct, 13th and 14th in two one-off ties. Division of Honour: top two up direct, 3rd and 4th in those ties. Four places, two of them contested; if both top-flight clubs win, only two clubs change level.

A1 Semi-Pro: top two promoted. Super League: bottom two relegated. In practice the bottom places are decided by MFL licensing, not form - in both 2025-26 and 2026-27 clubs were ejected for failing the national licence - and reserve/feeder sides cannot go up.

National Amateur League I top two go up; Challenge League bottom two go down into it.

No sporting route in either direction. Atlante's arrival in 2026-27 came from buying Mazatlán's franchise, not from promotion.

Eliteserien: 15th-16th direct, 14th in a two-legged play-off. OBOS: top 2 direct, 3rd-6th single-leg ladder; the ladder winner meets the Eliteserien 14th. One place is contested, so the loser stays at its level.

Ekstraklasa 16th-18th relegated. 1 Liga 1st-2nd promoted directly, 3rd-6th play off for the third place.

The four runners-up enter a two-round play-off: round 1 is a single match with the fixed bracket gr. I v gr. III and gr. IV v gr. II; round 2 is two legs against the 13th and 14th of 2 Liga (II-liga club hosts the second leg). Each tie won by a runner-up swaps one club, so 0-2 extra promotions and 0-2 extra relegations. Group placement is territorial by voivodeship, not a fixed membership; a group that receives a relegated II-liga club sends one extra club down to IV liga (5 instead of 4) to stay at 18. Audited total: the floor of the stated range.

2 direct in each direction (top 2 of Liga Portugal 2 up, 17th-18th of the Primeira Liga down) plus one shared two-legged tie: 16th of the Primeira Liga v 3rd of Liga Portugal 2. One club moves through that tie, so 3 up and 3 down are not independent.
2 direct (promotion-stage 1st and 2nd up; Liga Portugal 2 17th-18th down) plus one shared two-legged tie: 3rd of the Liga 3 promotion stage v 16th of Liga Portugal 2.

Up from the Campeonato de Portugal: top 2 of each of the two promotion groups (the groups are filled by the top 2 of each of the four geographic series). A club crossing this boundary is then placed in the north (Série A) or south (Série B) Liga 3 series, or in the Campeonato de Portugal series covering its district association.

QSL2 champion goes up directly, runner-up plays the QSL 11th in a single match; QSL 12th goes down directly and 11th risks the same play-off, so exactly one of {QSL 11th, QSL2 runner-up} is in the top flight next season.

Liga II play-off 1st and 2nd go up directly subject to eligibility; 3rd and 4th meet Liga I 13th and 14th in two-legged ties. Liga I 15th and 16th are relegated directly, 13th and 14th only if they lose. Promotion is closed to 12 of the 22 Liga II clubs in 2026-27 on legal-status/ownership grounds, so the direct places can pass down the play-off table. In 2026 only three clubs moved each way (two direct promotions plus Voluntari via the play-off).
Pro League: bottom 3 (16th-18th) relegated directly, no play-off. First Division: top 2 direct, 3rd-6th play off for the third place (single-leg ties).

League One champion up directly, 2nd-4th ladder winner meets the Championship 9th over two legs. Championship 10th down directly, 9th only through that tie.
League Two champion up directly, 2nd-4th ladder winner meets League One 9th over two legs. League One 10th down directly, 9th only through that tie.

From 2027-28 this should return to 2 up / 2 down. Steady state (2 up / 2 down): the game runs on the database snapshot of 14 clubs and must keep the roster size, so the one-off 2026-27 shrink (4 down / 2 up, 14 to 12) is recorded in this note but not applied. Applying it every season would shrink the league by two clubs a year.
II. Liga champion up directly (subject to licence); 2nd plays the Niké liga 11th over two legs. Niké liga 12th goes down directly, 11th only through that same tie, so one place moves through it.
2. SNL champion up directly, runner-up in a two-legged tie against the PrvaLiga 9th. PrvaLiga 10th down directly, 9th only through that tie. One shared place.

Superettan: top 2 direct, 3rd v 4th over two legs, that winner meets the Allsvenskan 14th over two legs. Allsvenskan: 15th-16th direct down, 14th only through the shared tie. One place moves through the play-off.
Ettan: each division winner goes up directly (2); each runner-up plays one of Superettan's 13th/14th over two legs (2 more). Superettan: 15th-16th direct down, 13th-14th only through those two ties.
Challenge League champion up directly, runner-up in a two-legged tie against the Super League 11th. Super League 12th down directly, 11th only through that tie. One shared place.
Simple 1-up/1-down: Promotion League champion (subject to licensing) replaces the Challenge League's bottom club. The Promotion League also relegates its bottom two to the regional 1. Liga Classic.
T2: champion and runner-up up directly, 3rd-6th play off for the third place. T1: bottom three relegated directly, no play-out.

Nominal shape is 2 direct + 2 play-off places each way (13th/14th vs 3rd/4th, two legs, plus 15th/16th down and champion/runner-up up). 2026-27 resolved as 3 up / 3 down: Bukovyna and Chornomorets up directly, Livyi Bereh won a play-off, Oleksandriya lost one; Poltava and Oleksandriya down, Rukh Lviv withdrew. Audited total: the floor of the stated range.

Druha Liha's two group winners go up (reserve sides ineligible), and the relegated Persha Liha clubs are placed in group A or B by geography. Downwards this is nominal: the PFL has not relegated Druha Liha clubs by table position since 2006-07, and the Persha Liha's relegation play-offs are irregular and were cancelled in 2025-26 - clubs leave by losing professional status or withdrawing.
First Division champion and runner-up go up; Pro League 13th and 14th go down. No play-off in either direction.

up is the total number of promotion slots and up_playoff is how many of them are decided by play-off: 2 direct (Segunda champion and runner-up) + 1 from the play-offs among 3rd-6th, which is why the Torneo Competencia winner matters. down=3, all direct from the Tabla de Descenso (two-season average), not from any single tournament table. 16 - 3 + 3 = 16 and 14 - 3 + 3 = 14, so sizes hold as long as the average table is computed on two seasons rather than on the current one.

Pro League 1st and 2nd up directly, 3rd into a single play-off at home against the Super League 12th; Super League bottom down directly. Counts flex: the Super League article says two or three clubs can be relegated, and promotion is voided if a reserve side wins the Pro League.

One promotion place and one relegation place. Relegation is decided on an aggregate table covering Apertura and Clausura (2025: Yaracuyanos last; 2026: Anzoategui already down). The promoted club comes through the second tier's final, so it is a play-off winner in practice.

Cymru North and Cymru South each send their champion up (licence required). The two runners-up meet in a one-off; that winner then plays the Cymru Premier 14th for the last top-flight place, so exactly one of {14th, tier-2 play-off winner} is in the league next season. 15th and 16th are relegated directly and are placed in North or South by geography.
LaLiga 2: top two promoted directly, 3rd-6th play off for the third place. LaLiga: bottom three relegated, no play-out.
Primera Federación: the two group champions go up directly and the two play-off winners join them. LaLiga 2: the bottom four are relegated.

Albania.real: 36 rounds plus announced Championship/Relegation rounds (top 6 / bottom 4)
Albania.note: Both the English and Albanian 2026-27 articles mark the split and link to sections that do not exist; neither gives a round count for it. Treated as an announcement, not a format.

Albania.real: 10th relegated directly, 9th plays the Kategoria e Pare play-off final loser
Albania.note: The Albanian league overview still states the old rule (bottom two down, no play-out); the 2026-27 Kategoria e Pare article describes the play-off for 9th.

Albania.real: 3 promoted (2 direct + 1 play-off) against 2 documented relegation places
Albania.note: The two directions cannot both be true for a 10-club league; the missing place is not documented in any source read.

Andorra.real: the league overview text describes 8 clubs, 21 rounds, a top-four/bottom-four split and 27 games
Andorra.note: That prose describes the pre-2020 eight-club format. The infobox (teams = 10) and the 2025-26 season article (ten clubs, three meetings, no split) are current and are what is recorded.

Argentina: ARGC is a phase, not a competition: the 2026 top division is Apertura + Clausura + aggregate table. The Apertura row (same 30 clubs) is missing, so the 'Campeon de Liga' title and one of the two relegation slots cannot be computed from the database.
Level-1 relegation is not resolvable from the ARGC row at all: it needs the season aggregate table (both tournaments) and a 2024-2026 promedio table, and 2024/2025 data is absent.

AR3F (18) and AR3R (19) are two paths of one 37-club competition (Torneo Federal A 2026), not two competitions. 18+19=37 is only the entry split after the first phase; clubs eliminated from the championship path are re-fed into the Revalida, so one club can appear in both rows within a season and the Revalida's final field exceeds 19.

Level 3 is two parallel branches, not one league: Torneo Federal A (37 clubs, indirectly affiliated) and Primera B Metropolitana (22 clubs, directly affiliated). The three level-3 rows sum to 59, which is the correct total, but treating those 59 as one league is wrong - clubs only cross branches through Primera Nacional relegation, by affiliation.
The level-3 downward edge is missing entirely (Federal A: 4 down; Primera B: 2 down). Without those rows, clubs relegated from level 3 have nowhere to go and level-3 sizes cannot be maintained.

Missing rows: Torneo Apertura 2026 (level 1, 30 clubs), Primera C Metropolitana (level 4, directly affiliated), Torneo Argentino del Interior 2027 / Torneo Regional Federal Amateur (level 4, indirectly affiliated).

Source conflict: the English Torneo Federal A page says 20 clubs entered the Revalida first phase; the Spanish page and arithmetic (37 - 18) give 19, which matches our row. The English page also says Federal A relegation goes to the Torneo Regional Federal Amateur, while the Spanish page (newer) says the Torneo Argentino del Interior, which replaces the TRFA as 4th tier from 2027.
Primera Nacional totals are stable but the branch split is not: 2026 relegated 3 to Primera B Metropolitana and 1 to Torneo Federal A. Any model that assigns a fixed 2/2 will break the branch sizes.

Armenia.note: The First League article gives teams = 16 but its current-season link points at 2025-26; no 2026-27 source exists yet. 15 is kept as our row, 16 as the last confirmed figure.

Australia: Level 2 is only partly represented: the database holds 2 of the 9 member-federation NPLs (NSW 16 + Victoria 14 = 30 clubs) out of roughly 110. Missing at level 2: NPL Queensland (12), NPL South Australia (12), NPL Western Australia (12), NPL Northern NSW (12), NPL Capital Football/ACT (11), NPL Tasmania (10) and the Northern Territory's NorZone Premier League (8).

A-League academy sides hold NPL slots that cannot climb: Sydney FC Youth and Western Sydney Wanderers Youth in NPL NSW (2 of 16), Melbourne City Youth in NPL Victoria (1 of 14). In NSW they are explicitly ineligible for the Australian Championship and finals. They can still go down (Central Coast Mariners Academy was relegated out of NPL NSW after 2025; Melbourne Victory Youth was relegated out of NPL Victoria after 2026), and Victoria even let Melbourne City Youth be promoted from VPL1 into NPL Victoria for 2026, so 'academy' blocks upward movement above NPL but not downward movement or intra-state promotion.

Licence withdrawal, not sport: Western United had their A-League licence removed by Football Australia for financial reasons before 2025-26, cutting the league from 13 to 12, and Western United Youth then folded out of Victoria Premier League 1 during 2026. A simulation must model A-League exits as licence events, since there is no relegation.

Expansion is pending but not for this season: Auckland FC entered in 2024-25 (making 13 before Western United's removal); the Canberra men's licence has slipped repeatedly and on 17 July 2026 was re-targeted at 2028-29, so 2026-27 stays at 12.

Calendar mismatch inside one 'season' label: the A-League runs 16 Oct 2026 - 5/6 Jun 2027, while NPL competitions run February - September in the same calendar year. A '2026-27' snapshot therefore pairs A-League 2026-27 with NPL 2026 (already finished, 13 Sep 2026) rather than NPL 2027.

Level-2 rows are parallel state leagues, not one national tier: there is no sporting movement between NPL NSW and NPL Victoria, and a club relocating states joins that state's pyramid through the annual declaration of leagues rather than by promotion or relegation, so a mover between A2SW and A2VI is not a pyramid move.

New South Wales publishes a 1 + play-off relegation model (not a fixed 2), so treat the NSW boundary as one automatic place plus a 0-or-1 play-off place; Victoria publishes a fixed 3 down / 2 + 1 up. Sizes are therefore stable at 16 and 14 but the number of movers per season is not identical.
Belgium: No level 4 in our rows: below BE3 sit Tweede afdeling / Division 2 Amateur (VV A, VV B, FFA). A club relegated from BE3A or BE3V has nowhere to land, so any simulation that runs a demotion must either stop at level 3 or add the level-4 rows.

Naming: the rows call level 3 '1ste Nationale FFA/VV'. The competition is Eerste nationale (Dutch) / Nationale 1 (French) / Belgian Division 1 (English); FFA and VV are the wings (Football Francophone Amateur / Voetbal Vlaanderen), not the competition name. 'FFA' is also not ACFF's current label everywhere - sources alternate between FFA and ACFF.

The two level-3 rows are parallel leagues at the same level, not a hierarchy: they must not be promoted/relegated into each other. The only cross-wing rule is that a level-3 club keeps the wing of its affiliation when it goes up or down.
BE2's size of 15 is a transition artefact, not a design target. Anyone assuming 16 or 18 (the Feb 2025 announcement said '16-18 depending on U23 results', later dropped) will get league sizes wrong.
BE1 in 2026-27 has no play-offs at all. Carrying over the 2023-24..2025-26 'split with rounds + play-offs' format (or phases such as PO1/PO2) would be wrong; the season is a plain 34-round table.

BE3A's format is not 'single': it is a split after 22 rounds with points halved for both the promotion and the relegation play-offs. Modelling it as one table loses the reset and the play-off promotion slot.

U23 reserve teams (Club NXT, Jong Genk, Jong KAA Gent, RSCA Futures in BE2; Jong Cercle, OH Leuven U23, Union SG U23, SL16 FC, Zebra Elites in level 3) are real members of the pyramid: always eligible for relegation, never for promotion. A promotion move onto a U23 club is invalid.

Relegation counts at level 3 are conditional, not fixed: BE3V drops 2 plus 0-2 more depending on how many VV-affiliated clubs come down from BE2, BE3A drops 2 plus possibly 1. Hard-coding 'bottom 2 down' at level 3 breaks the 16/12 sizes in seasons with same-wing double relegations.
Brazil: State championships run in parallel and are NOT a tier: the national pyramid (Série A-D) and the 27 state pyramids are two independent systems (en: 'Brazilian football league system'). Campeonato Paulista Série A1 2026 ran 10 Jan - 8 Mar while Série A ran 28 Jan - 2 Dec, so the same clubs are entered in both at once (e.g. Palmeiras, Corinthians, Santos, São Paulo, Red Bull Bragantino in both). A 'one club belongs to one league per season' model is therefore wrong for Brazil unless states are stored as a parallel competition, not a level.

State championships have their own promotion/relegation inside their own pyramid (Paulista A1 relegated Velo Clube and Ponte Preta to A2 in 2026), and their only structural link upward is qualification: state-league/state-cup places feed Série D entry (and the Copa do Brasil). No state title ever promotes a club into Série C or above.

A club cannot be in two national divisions in the same season: Série A, B, C and D are strictly disjoint (a Série A club is never also in B/C/D). The 'one league per season' invariant holds only within the national pyramid; across the state pyramid it does not.

Promotion/relegation between Série A and Série B is NOT the only structural movement: B<->C and C<->D also move clubs every year, so a model that only wires BRA1<->BRA2 will drop real clubs. Série B's bottom four go to Série C; Série C's top four go to Série B.

Série C and Série D exist below (20 and 96 clubs in 2026). 2026 is a transition year: Série C had only 2 relegated (Confiança, Itabaiana) instead of the usual 4, while 6 clubs came up from Série D (4 semi-finalists + 2 play-off winners among quarter-final losers), because Série C grows to 24 clubs in 2027 and 28 from 2028. So C->D = 2 and D->C = 6 in 2026, not the historical 4/4.

Série D has no relegation at all (pt infobox 'rebaixa' is empty; no downward edge exists). Its field is set by qualification: clubs relegated from Série C, state-league/state-cup qualifiers, clubs that reached the previous Série D second stage, and CBF-ranking fill-ups. A generic pyramid model that assumes every league has both an up and a down edge breaks at Série D.
Série B 2026 promotion is not a pure 'top N' rule: 2 of the 4 places are decided by a play-off among 3rd-6th, so a model that maps 'positions 1-4 promoted' produces the wrong set of clubs.

The season is a calendar year (late Jan - early Dec), not Aug-May, and 2026 had a FIFA World Cup pause (11 Jun - 19 Jul) plus the state-to-national handover in Jan-Apr; season-boundary logic copied from European leagues will mis-date every transfer between these divisions.

Bulgaria.note: The 2026-27 Second League has 20 clubs in a transitional season; it returns to 16 in 2027-28.

The English article says 14th-20th go down directly (six) and 13th plays off; the Bulgarian article says five direct relegations and 13th in a play-off. Six is used here because it matches the positions named.

Chile: CL2F and CL2Z are not leagues. Both are stages of the single level-3 competition (Liga de Segunda): CL2F is 'Fase 2', the split into the Liguilla de Ascenso and Liguilla de Descenso; CL2Z is a zonal stage/qualifier of the same competition, not a play-off group with its own 2 clubs. The database has turned one competition's phases into three level-? leagues.

CL2F's size 12 matches no current level-3 format: 2026 has 14 clubs whose Fase 2 groups hold 7 each, and 2025 was a single 13-club table. The last 12-club second phase was 2016-17 (zonal phase, then a 12-club national phase), so the number is a stale historical format and is dropped here instead of copied into a league size.
CL2Z's size 2 is not a club count at all; it is the number of zones (Norte/Sur) / a two-club zonal qualifier, so a 2-club 'league' would break any table generation.

The three fragments (CL2F 12, CL2Z 2) leave the actual level 3 without a row of the right size (14), so promotion from level 2 (1 club) and relegation to level 4 (2 clubs) currently have no valid destination.
Level 4 (Tercera División A, 14 clubs) is missing, so the 2 clubs relegated from level 3 have nowhere to go.
The rows describe a flat single-table league; from 2026 level 3 resets into two 7-club liguillas mid-season, so its schedule and table structure cannot be modelled as one 14-team round robin.

China.real: one 24-club China League Two whose first stage is two geographic zones (North 12, South 12)

China.real: 2 up / 2 direct down + 14th in a two-leg play-off
China.note: '2 up / 2.5 down' is new for 2026; a stored 2025 shape (2 down, no play-off) is stale.
Total is right by construction; do not treat the two rows as independent 12-club leagues when generating fixtures.

Chinese Taipei.topic: No relegation from the 2026-27 top flight
Chinese Taipei.detail: The TFPL has eight clubs and normally relegates 8th directly and sends 7th to a play-off against the League 2 runner-up. For 2026-27 only, the CFA decided there would be no relegations because the league expands for 2027-28. A sim that always relegates the bottom club will be wrong for this season.

Chinese Taipei.topic: League 2 promotes two, not one plus a play-off
Chinese Taipei.detail: Because of the same expansion, the 2026-27 League 2 table marks 1st and 2nd as promoted (both green). The normal route is champion only, with the runner-up in the promotion/relegation play-off.

Our row says 10, which is right for 2026-27 (the league expanded from eight). The competition-format prose on the league page still describes eight clubs and 14 games; the 2026-27 season article (10 clubs, 18 games) is the correct source.
Below League 2 clubs enter through pre-season qualifiers and can withdraw (three clubs did not enter for 2026-27), so there is no bottom-club relegation to model.

Colombia.topic: A single row per league, but two championships per season
Colombia.detail: COL1 is stored as one league, but the Colombian top flight runs two independent tournaments (Apertura and Finalizacion), each with its own champion and its own semi-final groups and final. The row name 'Liga Dimayor Finalizacion' names only the second half. Fixtures, form and the title race reset in July.

Colombia.topic: Relegation is not decided by the season table
Colombia.detail: The bottom two are relegated on a three-season average of first-stage points (promedio). A newly promoted club carries only its own seasons in the average, which is why the rule historically protected big clubs.

Since 2025, how the two Primera B promotions are decided depends on where the two short-tournament winners finish in the aggregate table (four scenarios, ranging from both direct to a grand final plus a play-off). The count (2) is fixed; the route is not.
The second tier's infobox has no relegation, and no club drops out of the professional pyramid from it. It is therefore closed downwards even though Primera C exists as an amateur/regional level.

Costa Rica.topic: Single row, but two tournaments and a grand final
Costa Rica.detail: CRPD is stored as one league. In reality the season is Apertura + Clausura, each 18 rounds plus a four-team knockout and a possible grand final, with two titles. Treating the row as one 36-round table (the older 12-club description) gives the wrong fixtures.

Costa Rica.topic: The league page still says 22 matchdays
Costa Rica.detail: The Liga FPD format prose describes a double round-robin of 22 matchdays, which was the 12-club shape. Since 2025-26 the league has ten clubs and an 18-match regular phase; the 2025-26 season article is the correct source.

Costa Rica.topic: Ten clubs is recent and partly administrative
Costa Rica.detail: The league dropped from 12 to 10 for 2025-26 after Guanacasteca and Santos de Guapiles had their licences revoked. A sim seeded with older data will show 12.

Costa Rica.topic: Closed downwards by our data, not by reality
Costa Rica.detail: One club is relegated each season on the aggregate Apertura+Clausura table, to the Liga de Ascenso. That league is not in our list, so the report marks the direction closed (per the task rule for single-row countries).

Croatia.detail: The HNL table marks only 10th as relegated. Older Croatian seasons used a 9th-place play-off against the second tier; that is not the current rule, so a sim that adds one will invent a fixture.
The Prva NL had 12 clubs from 2022-23 to 2025-26 and expanded to 16 for 2026-27. Our row says 16, which is correct for this season and wrong for last season.

Croatia.topic: Reserve team in the second tier
Croatia.detail: Dinamo Zagreb II plays in the Prva NL 2026-27 and cannot be promoted to the HNL (farm teams must stay at least one level below the senior side). The champion is promoted only if eligible; a second-placed finisher takes the place.

Croatia.topic: The HNL is a quadruple round-robin
Croatia.detail: With 10 clubs the HNL plays 36 matches (four meetings), not the 33 of the old 12-club triple round-robin. The 180 matches per season confirm 36 per club.

Cyprus.topic: Asymmetric split in the top flight
Cyprus.detail: The First Division does not split into two equal groups: the top six play a double round-robin (10 more games, 36 total) while the bottom eight play a single round-robin (7 more, 33 total). A single round count for the division only fits one of the two groups.

Cyprus.topic: Second Division points carry and it plays 29 games
Cyprus.detail: The 16 clubs play each other once (15 rounds), then split into two groups of eight that each play a double round-robin (14 more). Points and goals are carried (the 2025-26 tables start with the first-phase points). A naive 'two groups of eight, 7 rounds' reading underestimates the season by half.

Cyprus.topic: No play-offs anywhere in the modelled pyramid
Cyprus.detail: Both divisions decide promotion and relegation by table position after the split; there is no promotion/relegation play-off in either direction.

Cyprus.topic: Top flight has no relegation play-off
Cyprus.detail: The bottom three of Group B are relegated directly; 12th is not spared by a play-off.

Czech Republic.note: The size is right; the shape is not. It is one division split into two 16-team groups whose winners meet in a two-leg baráž for a single promotion place.
The split is three-way, not two-way. Places 7-10 play a two-legged placement bracket (7v10, 8v9, final), not a relegation group.

Czech Republic.ours: two parallel leagues: Bohemian and Moravian-Silesian
Czech Republic.note: There are two level-3 competitions but three groups. Our CZ3C row bundles the two Bohemian groups; CZ3M is the single Moravian-Silesian league.
Any model that relegates a flat bottom 3 from the Chance Liga is wrong for this format.

Denmark.topic: Every level is a split competition
Denmark.detail: All four divisions are 12 clubs, 22 rounds, then a top-six promotion/championship group and a bottom-six relegation group of 10 more rounds (32 in total), with points carried. None of them is a plain double round-robin; a 'single, rounds: 22' model produces half a season.

Denmark.topic: The 3. Division relegates four, not two
Denmark.detail: The fourth tier's relegation group has six clubs and the bottom four go down to the Denmark Series; only two survive. That is a much steeper cut than at levels 1-3, where two go down.

Denmark.topic: No relegation play-off in the Superliga any more
Denmark.detail: The 2016-17 to 2018-19 format had a multi-step relegation play-off involving 1. Division clubs. Since the 12-club format (2019-20 onward) the bottom two of the qualifying playoff are relegated directly, which is what the 2025-26 relegation list (Fredericia 11th, Vejle 12th) shows.

Denmark.topic: Our ids name only one group of a split
Denmark.detail: DK3O ('2.Division') and DK4L ('3.Division') are the third and fourth tiers, not groups; the id suffixes look like geography but Denmark is a single national division at every modelled level.

Ecuador.topic: Serie A is one season with three final groups, not Apertura/Clausura
Ecuador.detail: The 2026 format is a 30-round first stage followed by a championship hexagonal (6), a Copa Sudamericana quadrangular (4) and a relegation hexagonal (6). There are no two separate championships; the single champion comes from the hexagonal.

Ecuador.topic: Relegation is decided in a six-team mini-league
Ecuador.detail: The bottom six carry their 30-match records into a 10-match relegation hexagonal, and its bottom two go down. A club can be bottom of the 30-round table and survive, or mid-table and be dragged down.

Ecuador.topic: The Serie B article describes an older format
Ecuador.detail: The Serie B league page's prose still says 'top four after both stages ... playoffs'. The 2025 season (and the 2026 field) uses a 22-round first stage plus a six-team promotion round and a six-team relegation round, with points carried. The 2025 season tables are the evidence.

Ecuador.topic: Reserve team in the promotion race
Ecuador.detail: Independiente Juniors plays in Serie B and is ineligible for promotion; in 2025 it finished 3rd in the promotion round and the place went to the next eligible club. A naive top-two promotion will promote it.

Egypt.topic: The league article still describes the old 18-club season
Egypt.detail: The competition-format prose says '18 clubs ... 34 games ... three lowest-placed teams are relegated' and cites a format 'since 2015'. The 2026-27 season is the first with 20 clubs and a two-phase split (19 rounds, then 6 + 14), with four relegated; the infobox and the 2026-27 team list already show 20.
The league expanded from 18 to 20 for 2026-27 (three promoted from the Second Division A, one extra place from the reshuffle). Our row says 20, which is right for this season and wrong for 2025-26.
Unlike the old double round-robin, the 2026-27 first phase is one match per opponent (19 games), then the table splits. A sim that keeps a 38-round table will overplay the season by half.

The 2026-27 article says the league 'splits into two groups' but does not say whether first-phase points are carried. `points_carry` is left null rather than guessed; the usual Egyptian split practice is to carry them, but this is a new format with no completed season to check.

Egypt.topic: Four relegated from a single row
Egypt.detail: Because EGY1 is the only Egyptian league in our list, the direction is closed in the report even though four clubs actually go down to the Second Division A.

Estonia.topic: Reserve teams are ineligible for promotion
Estonia.detail: Esiliiga 2026 contains Flora U21, Levadia U21, Nomme Kalju U21 and Nomme United U21; Esiliiga B contains several more U21 sides. None can be promoted to the Meistriliiga. A sim that promotes the top two of the Esiliiga will promote an ineligible club whenever a U21 side finishes there.

Estonia.topic: Each boundary moves three clubs down but only two up directly
Estonia.detail: The Esiliiga sends 10th and 9th down directly and its 8th to a play-off; the Esiliiga B sends 1st and 2nd up directly and its 3rd to a play-off. The mismatch is real: the play-offs are separate ties (Esiliiga 8th v Esiliiga B 3rd, and Meistriliiga 9th v Esiliiga 2nd), so the number of clubs crossing each boundary is 3/3 but only two of each are automatic.

Estonia.topic: All three levels are 10 clubs and 36 games
Estonia.detail: The pyramid is unusually uniform: 10 clubs, four meetings, 36 matches at levels 1-3. The differences are only in promotion/relegation rules, not in size.

Esiliiga promotion to the Meistriliiga requires the Meistriliiga licence; the champion can be passed over, with the place going to the next eligible club. The source states this explicitly rather than as an exception.

Ethiopia.topic: Our row says 18, the league now has 20
Ethiopia.detail: 2024-25 was an 18-club season (18-team table, two relegated). The league expanded to 20 for 2025-26 and the league's own infobox and format section now describe 20 clubs and 38 games. Our row is one season stale.

The 2026-27 season has started (November 2026) but has no Wikipedia article, so the 2026-27 size of 20 is inferred from the league page describing the current (2025-26) season as 20 clubs. It is not confirmed by a 2026-27 club list.

Ethiopia.topic: Single row, so closed both ways
Ethiopia.detail: Three clubs are relegated to the Ethiopian Higher League each season, but that league is not in our data, so the report marks the downward direction closed.

Faroe Islands.detail: 1. deild is mostly reserve sides. A reserve team cannot be promoted, and there is only relegation from the top flight if at least one non-reserve club finishes in the 1. deild top three. If the top two are both reserve sides, the third-placed eligible club comes up instead.

If a club is relegated from the Premier League and already has a reserve team in 1. deild, the reserve team is moved down a division to make room. That can save another club from relegation, so the nominal 2 down / 2 up is not always 2/2 in practice.

Both levels are 10 clubs playing each other three times (27 matches), with the extra home games drawn before the season rather than decided by the previous table. A double round-robin model (18) understates the season by a third.

Finland.real: Kolmonen is 10 regional groups (110 clubs); KOG2 is the Uusimaa 'Etelä-Suomi lohko B' of 12
Finland.note: Size and level are right for that group, but the group is one of ten and its winner must win a promotion play-off to reach Kakkonen.

Finland.real: Kakkonen (level 4): 30 clubs in three groups of 10, double round robin then a championship/relegation split
Finland.note: Our rows jump from Ykkönen (t3) to Kolmonen (t5). Kakkonen is the missing link: FIYK relegates into it and KOG2 promotes into it, so no boundary between our t3 and t5 rows can be encoded without it.

France.note: National 1 is 48 clubs in 3 groups of 16 (30 rounds). Our 16/16/17 gives 49; group C is one club too large.

Name is correct only from 2026-27: the former Championnat National was rebranded Ligue 3 (FFF competition rules 'Ligue 3 - règlement 2026-2027'). Older rows named 'Championnat National' would be wrong at level 3.
Our level 5 carries only groups E, F and G; five groups are missing. Sizes (14) are correct.

Germany.note: Regionalliga Nord (18) and Regionalliga West (18) are missing from our data. The three we carry have correct sizes: Bayern 19, Nordost 18, Südwest 18.
Id reads like 'Nord' but holds Nordost. The newly added Regionalliga Nord uses id RLN; if ids are regenerated, prefer RLNO for Nordost.
Correct, and it implies 38 rounds (380 matches).

Gibraltar.note: The Gibraltar Reserves Division was replaced by the Intermediate League in June 2018. It is a development competition: squads of up to 18, at least 13 players eligible for Gibraltar, at most 5 over the age of 23, plus a salary cap. No promotion route.
Our 9 could not be confirmed from the sources used; the Intermediate League's entry varies with which GFL clubs field a side. Left at our value rather than guessed.

Greece.real: one group of 16 in 2026-27, but two groups (North/South) in 2025-26
Greece.note: The single group is new: the 2025-26 edition was split into a north and a south group, each with its own champion (Iraklis and Kalamata both went up). The reduction to 16 clubs in one group also removed the promotion play-offs and relegation play-outs.

Hong Kong.real: 16 clubs in 2026-27, split 8/8; the competition-format text describes an 8+7 split because it was written for a 15-club season
Hong Kong.note: The single-round-robin-then-split shape is right; the group sizes follow the entry list, so they change with promotions and withdrawals.

No HKFA U22 league article could be found; the HKFA runs age-group competitions alongside the senior pyramid (the U22-minute quota used to be enforced through the Sapling Cup, discontinued after 2025-26). Treat the row as an age-group competition with no promotion route; size 11 is our value, unverified.

Hungary.real: champion up, runner-up into a one-legged play-off against the NB I 11th (new for 2026-27)
Hungary.note: The NB II article still describes the previous rule - top two promoted, NB I 11th and 12th relegated. The 2026-27 NB I page and the Hungarian season page both confirm the new single-match play-off, so that is what is recorded here.

India.real: 8 clubs, but the season article does not state the round structure
India.note: Rounds left null rather than assumed. The 2025-26 edition was a single table; whether 2026-27 is one or two round robins is not documented yet.

India.real: I-League 3 is the fourth national tier; state leagues are the fifth
India.note: India now has four national divisions plus state leagues. Our rows stop at I-League 2, so its two relegation places have no destination in the dataset.

Indonesia.real: 24 clubs, group structure for 2026-27 not yet published
Indonesia.note: 2024-25 used two groups of eight with a championship round and relegation play-offs; with 24 clubs the shape must differ. Recorded with null group count rather than a guess.

Indonesia.real: no title play-off section in the 2026-27 season article; 2024-25 had a Championship Series
Indonesia.note: The 2026-27 Super League appears to be a straight 34-round table, but the format has changed twice in three seasons, so treat 'no title play-off' as season-specific.

Iran.real: the 2026-27 table legend marks 15th-18th as relegation (four places), but only three clubs came up from the Azadegan League
Iran.note: Recorded as three down (two direct plus the 14th in a play-off), which fits the three-club Azadegan intake. The four-place legend cannot be reconciled with a stable 18-club league, and the 2025-26 season is no guide because the league was expanding then: only Mes Rafsanjan went down, through the play-off, while three clubs came up.

Iran.real: the general League 2 article says the top two of each group go up (four clubs); the current Azadegan intake shows three
Iran.note: The four-club rule is older. The 2026-27 Azadegan article names exactly three promoted clubs - the League 2 champion, the runner-up and the play-off winner - so the three-place model is recorded.

Israel: Liga Leumit's own article still says points are halved and the split is played as a single round-robin, which is the pre-2013 description; the 2025-26 season tables show full points carried (37 matches, e.g. 18W-13D-6L = 67 pts) and both eight-team groups playing once. The season tables are used here.

The Israeli Premier League all-time table lists one '13th place' relegation play-off, and older seasons did use one; the 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons all relegated exactly the bottom two with no play-off, so the 2026-27 model uses 2 down / 0 play-off.

Italy.real: one 60-club Serie C with 3 geographical groups of 20
Italy.note: Sizes and levels are correct, but the three rows share one promotion play-off, one relegation play-out and a yearly geographical re-draw of clubs between groups. Do not treat them as closed leagues with a fixed 1-up-1-down each.

Jamaica: The 2026-27 season infobox says 247 matches, which cannot be right for 14 clubs playing 39 matches each (273 in total); the round count and the 39-match statement are used.
Kazakhstan: The English 2026 Premier League article is tagged AI-generated and its attendance figure is meaningless, but its 16-team, 30-round, 240-match, 2-relegated shape matches the Russian Wikipedia article exactly, so the numbers are used.

Kazakhstan's second tier is variously called First League / First Division / Pervaya Liga; the Wikipedia article title is 'Kazakhstan First Division' while the league is 'Pervaya Liga'. Same competition.
Latvia: The 2026 Virsliga infobox says 170 matches, but 10 clubs playing four rounds is 180; the round count (four rounds, 36 per club) is stated in prose and matches the LFF regulations cited there, so 36 is used.

Our row's name 'Futbola Pirmā līga' is the pre-2021 name: the second tier has been branded Nakotnes liga / Future League since 2021 and LVBET League for sponsorship in 2026. Same competition, id unchanged.
Lebanon: The 2026-27 season article says both that the league is 'divided into two groups of six' and that 'the top four teams enter the championship group, while the bottom four enter the relegation group'. The two sentences cannot both be true for 12 clubs. The 'groups of six' reading is used because the same paragraph says each club plays 'the other five clubs in its group twice, for a further 10 matches', which only works with two groups of six, and because 2024-25 and 2025-26 both used a 6/6 split.

Points: the 2026-27 article says each club carries over half its points (rounded up); 2024-25 and 2025-26 say the same, so half-carry is used. This is why points_carry is true but the values are halved, not carried in full.
Libya: The Wikipedia league article still describes 36 clubs in 4 groups (its infobox and lead), which was the shape in earlier seasons. The LFF approved a 28-club, 2-group format for 2026-27 (Libya Observer, 21 September 2026), and Transfermarkt's 2026-27 tables show exactly two groups of 14. Our row's size 28 is right for 2026-27 and the 36/4 figure is stale.

Lithuania.note: The I Lyga infobox still says 16 clubs, but the approved 2026 participant list on the same page has 18 (including six B teams). Used 18 for the season.
Correct: the A Lyga was renamed TOPLYGA from 2026. Only the capitalisation differs.

Malaysia.note: Malaysia no longer runs a calendar-year league: 2025-26 ran 8 Aug 2025 - 17 May 2026 and 2026-27 runs 28 Aug 2026 - 23 May 2027. The Super League also had 13 clubs in 2025-26 and 12 in 2026-27, so our size 12 is right for the coming season only.

Malta.real: Maltese Premier League (Opening Round is one half of its season)
Malta.note: The league is a single competition of 12 clubs split into an Opening Round and a Closing Round, each with its own table and its own champion; points reset to zero between them. 'Opening Round' is not the league's name.
The Amateur League I had 14 clubs in 2025-26 (26 rounds) and drops to 12 for 2026-27 (22 rounds) after four relegations. Our 12 matches the coming season.

Mexico.real: none in practice, but legally contested
Mexico.note: The CAS ordered relegation back for 2026-27; Liga MX ignored it and made itself a closed league in July 2026, and the FMF's August 2026 model keeps Liga MX closed while restoring promotion between Liga de Expansión and Liga Premier. A Mexican Senate bill (Sep 2026) would force promotion back. Treat as closed for now, with political risk.
The Liga de Expansión MX article's format paragraph says '15 clubs' while its own 2026-27 participant list and infobox say 16. Used 16.

Mexico.ours: Liga MX Apertura / Liga de Expansión MX Clausura / U19 Apertura / U21 Apertura
Mexico.real: Liga MX, Liga de Expansión MX, Liga MX Sub-19, Liga MX Sub-21
Mexico.note: All four are year-round competitions split into Apertura and Clausura; the row names carry one tournament, not the competition.

Moldova.note: The Liga 1 infobox says 12 clubs, but the 2026-27 participant list and Phase I groups (6 + 5) have 11. Used 11 for the season.

Myanmar.note: The M League now runs August to May with 22 matches per club; the 2026-27 season is the current one. The old calendar-year habit dates from the Myanmar National League era.
Correct: the MNL was rebranded as M League in August 2026, with a new logo and trophy. Sponsor name Grand Royal M League.

Netherlands.note: The Eerste Divisie has had no sporting relegation since 2022 (KNVB suspension for 5-10 seasons). A Tweede Divisie amateur champion is not promoted; 2025-26 champions Quick Boys stayed put.

Netherlands.real: Derde Divisie A (one of two level-4 divisions)
Netherlands.note: The id is opaque but the mapping is right. Level 4 is two parallel divisions, A and B, 18 clubs each; we carry only A.

New Zealand: All three rows are marked level 1. They are the level-2 regional stage: the pyramid has exactly one level-1 competition (the National League Championship) and three parallel level-2 leagues.
The real level 1 (National League Championship, 11 clubs) is missing from the database entirely, so the top of this pyramid has no row.

The three level-2 rows are parallel, not a hierarchy: their club pools are disjoint (north / centre / south of the country) and clubs never move between them. A simulation that treats them as 1st/1st/1st of one ladder, or that promotes between them, is wrong.
The names hide the competition format: 'National League - North/Central/South' are the regional leagues that feed the National League, not national divisions of it.
Nothing records the fixed 4/3/2 qualifying quota or the two automatic reserve entrants (Auckland FC Reserves, Wellington Phoenix Reserves), which are the reason level 1 has 11 clubs rather than 9.
The 2027 restructure (12-club national double round robin, summer phase scrapped) is already announced; the rows describe the 2021-2026 format only.

Nicaragua.note: The competition's official name is Segunda División de Nicaragua; the league and Transfermarkt both brand it 'Liga de Ascenso'. Our name is the branded one, and our id NC2A matches that branding.

Nigeria.real: Nigeria Premier Football League (renamed 2023; the 2026-27 edition is branded Euromatch Premier Football League)
Nigeria.note: Same competition and same 20-club format; only the name in our row is the pre-2023 one.

North Macedonia.real: the league article still says the opponent is the winner of a tie between the two Second League group runners-up
North Macedonia.note: Outdated: the Second League has been a single division since 2021-22 and its 2026-27 table marks 3rd place as the play-off entrant. Use 1. MFL 8th v 2. MFL 3rd.

Norway.note: The PostNord sponsorship ran 2016-2025 only; from 2026 the league has no title sponsor. Level, size (14+14) and id mapping are correct.

Oman.real: Oman Professional League (Omantel Professional League for sponsorship)
Oman.note: No source read uses 'Jindal'. Probably a 2026-27 title sponsor that is not documented, or a bad name in our database.

Oman.real: the league page's own 2024-25 club list names only 12 clubs
Oman.note: The named list is stale (it still mentions 2023-24 relegations); the infobox says 14. 14 used.

Philippines.real: the 2026-27 league table labels places 1-5 'Championship round' and 6-10 'Classification round', implying a split that no text describes
Philippines.note: Unresolved: the stated format is a double round-robin of 20 games and the 2025-26 title was decided on the single table. Recorded as single; re-check if a PFF regulation appears.

Poland.topic: Level 4 is one competition, not four leagues
Poland.detail: PL31-PL34 are the four territorial groups of a single III liga (72 clubs). Clubs are re-placed between groups every season by voivodeship, and the play-off for promotion pairs groups against each other. Modelling the four rows as independent closed leagues with a fixed 1-up-1-down each is wrong: they share one promotion play-off and their relegation counts vary.

Poland.topic: 3-4 boundary is not a fixed number
Poland.detail: 4 direct promotions (group champions) + 0-2 from the runners-up play-off; 4 direct relegations + 0-2 from the same ties. JSON stores the maximum 6 with the 2 variable places marked as playoff places; read 4 as the guaranteed floor.

Legia II Warszawa and Śląsk II Wrocław play in 2 Liga. No reserve team has ever played in the Polish second tier and the historical rule barred reserve teams of Ekstraklasa/1 Liga clubs from promotion to 1 Liga. Treat their promotion to level 2 as blocked, but confirm against the 2026-27 PZPN regulation before hard-coding.

Portugal.topic: Liga 3 is not a single 20-club table
Portugal.detail: PT3A is stored as one league of 20 at level 3. In reality it is two geographic series of 10 (18 rounds) that then split: top 4 of each into a single 14-round promotion stage, positions 5-10 into two 6-club relegation series (10 rounds). Treating it as one table with 34 rounds and 3 relegations produces wrong fixtures and wrong promotion places (2 direct + 1 play-off, not 3 down).

Portugal.topic: Points carry differently in the two second phases
Portugal.detail: Nothing carries into the Liga 3 promotion stage (verified on the completed 2025-26 stage: 8 clubs, 14 matches each, no bonus). The relegation stage starts with bonus points 9 down to 1 based on first-stage position. A single boolean cannot express this; JSON keeps points_carry=false for the promotion path and documents the relegation bonus in stages.

Portugal.topic: Campeonato de Portugal promotion is not 'series winners go up'
Portugal.detail: Top 2 of each of the four series (8 clubs) advance to two groups of four; only the top 2 of each group (4 clubs) are promoted. Four clubs also come down from Liga 3, so the level 3-4 boundary is a fixed 4/4 with no play-off.

Portugal.topic: Levels 1-2 share a single play-off slot
Portugal.detail: 16th of the Primeira Liga v 3rd of Liga Portugal 2 is one two-legged tie that decides one promotion and one relegation. Counting it as a separate up-place and down-place double-counts the movement.

Sporting B, Benfica B and Porto B play in Liga Portugal 2 and cannot be promoted to the Primeira Liga (they can be relegated, and go down automatically if the senior side is). A naive top-2 promotion rule will promote an ineligible club.

Portugal.topic: Source disagreement on Liga Portugal 2 promotion places
Portugal.detail: The 2026-27 English Wikipedia standings mark result1=PL, result3=PL, result5=PO, which contradicts the Portuguese prose (top 2 promoted, 3rd to the play-off). The prose is used here; the wiki table looks mis-keyed.

Portugal.topic: Campeonato de Portugal relegation line changed in 2026-27
Portugal.detail: 2025-26: bottom five of each series (10th-14th) relegated directly, 20 clubs in total. 2026-27: 13th-14th direct, 11th-12th to relegation play-offs. Below the modelled floor (level 4 -> district championships), recorded as a note only. District intake is not fixed (24 in 2025-26, 20 in 2026-27).

Puerto Rico.real: the season article says each tournament is 'contested by eight teams'
Puerto Rico.note: The participating-club list and the standings both show nine clubs; the 'eight' looks like a leftover from 2025-26. 9 used.

Qatar.note: Confirmed by the English 2026-27 club list and by the Spanish and Arabic league articles, both of which say eight. Our 12 looks like a copy of the QSL figure.

Qatar.real: the English article says the champion plays the 10th-placed QSL club and the runner-up is not mentioned
Qatar.note: Outdated 2022-23 rule. The 2026-27 QSL table marks 11th as the play-off place and the Arabic article describes runner-up v second-last. Current shape used.

Qatar.ours: no relegation from the second tier
Qatar.real: the English infobox lists relegation to a 'Qatar Stars League 3', while its own body text and the Spanish/Arabic articles say there is no relegation and no third tier
Qatar.note: No QSL3 season or club list was found. Either way the destination is outside our data, so QU2L is closed_down.

Romania.note: The 2026-27 Liga II article says 'twenty-two teams' twice and its league table's team list contains 22 clubs. Our 23 does not match any reading of the sources.

Russia: 2DVB is one row for 4 parallel leagues: the 2026 Division B is 59 clubs in 4 geographic groups (Group 1: 16, Group 2: 15, Group 3: 16, Group 4: 12), each with its own champion, its own single promotion place and its own relegation quota (1 / 2 / 2 / 2). Group 4 additionally splits into subgroups 4A/4B after its summer stage. One row can only hold the aggregate.

Season phase: Division B runs March-November on a calendar-year cycle (2026 season), while RU1/RU2/R3D1 run July-June (2026/27). There is no 2026-27 Division B season, so the row's season label points at the 2026 season, which overlaps but does not coincide.

R3D1 'Phase 1' is not a phase of a league, it is one stage of a single competition: Division A is played as an autumn first stage (17 clubs: 10 gold + 7 silver, because Chernomorets, Chayka and Kuban failed licensing) and a spring second stage (20 clubs: 2x10, after 4 clubs come up from Division B and 1 goes down). The gold/silver split and the mid-season 4-in/1-out rotation cannot be expressed by one row.
Promotion from Division B to Division A happens in the winter (November/March), not at the end of the season, so end-of-season-only rotation logic places the 4 promoted clubs half a season late.

There is no relegation from Division A or promotion to it at the end of 2026-27; the FNL moved the A/B rotation to the winter window. A model that demotes the 2 bottom clubs in June 2027 would be wrong.

The bottom edge of the pyramid is missing: Division B relegates to the amateur Third League (tier 5, no row in our DB) and entry is by licensing application, not automatic promotion - 7 clubs left Division B for tier 5 at the end of 2026 (Dynamo-2 Makhachkala, Iskra, Irkutsk, Arsenal-2, Kvant, Ural-2, Chelyabinsk-2).
Naming: '1.Division' is the pre-2022 name of RU2; since 2022 it is the First League (Первая лига), just as the old '2. Division' became Second League Division A/B in 2023.

San Marino.topic: Who takes the second European place
San Marino.detail: The Italian league article says the 2nd-placed club qualifies for the Conference League; the English 2025-26 season article says the winner of the 2-11 play-off qualifies. The play-off exists either way; only its prize differs.

San Marino.topic: San Marino Academy U22 is not an ordinary club
San Marino.detail: One of the 16 participants is the federation's U22 academy side. It is a full member of the table and can finish anywhere, including 1st, but it is not a normal club that could be promoted or relegated.

Serbia.topic: Promotion and relegation are not balanced in 2026-27
Serbia.detail: SuperLiga: 14 clubs now, 12 from 2027-28, therefore 4 relegated (11th-14th). First League: still 16 clubs, promoting only 2 champions/runners-up but relegating 6 (11th-16th) to the Srpska liga. Any generic 3-up/3-down assumption is wrong for both levels this season.

SuperLiga splits 6 + 8 (31 vs 33 matches per club); First League splits 6 + 10 (35 vs 39). Points carry over, and the two groups are separate final tables, so 'one table of N clubs' cannot express either league.
SB19 (Omladinska liga Srbije) has no Wikipedia article; our 14 clubs could not be confirmed. Recorded as-is and flagged rather than guessed or nulled.

Singapore.topic: League article vs season article on the number of meetings
Singapore.detail: The Singapore Premier League article says eight clubs play four rounds (28 matches each, 112 total); the 2025-26 season article and its rule-change list say each team plays the others three times (21 matches). Both are right for their own season: 2025-26 was 21 rounds, 2026-27 is 28 (the fixture module encodes two home and two away legs).

SPL2 is the reserve league for SPL clubs (one second team per club), not the country's second division. The real level 2 is the Singapore Football League, which is not in our database. SPL2 cannot feed the SPL.

Singapore.topic: No promotion or relegation at all
Singapore.detail: SPL clubs are admitted by FAS invitation; there is no sporting route up from the SFL and none down. Any generic 1-up/1-down logic must be disabled for Singapore.

Slovakia.detail: SK19 (I. liga staršieho dorastu, U19) has no usable public table; our 14 clubs could not be confirmed. Kept as-is and flagged rather than guessed.
The II. Liga champion is promoted only if it meets the league's requirements; a licensed lower-placed club can take the place. Promotion is not purely sporting.

Spain: Segunda Federacion really has FIVE groups (I-V, 18 clubs each, 90 in total); our list holds only four (E4G2-E4G5), so Grupo I - the north-west group (Galicia, Asturias, Cantabria, Castilla y Leon) - is missing: 18 clubs, one fifth of level 4, with no row and no edges.

Because SF-I is absent, one fifth of every level-4 flow has no edge: in 2026-27 SF-I sent 2 clubs up to Primera Federacion (champion Deportivo Fabril + a play-off winner) and took 1 of the 10 clubs relegated from Primera Federacion (Ourense CF). Level 4 upward total is 10, not 8; downward total is 10, not 7.
Tier sizes differ by design: LaLiga 20, LaLiga2 22, Primera Federacion 2x20, Segunda Federacion 5x18. Any code assuming one uniform size per tier is wrong for ES2 (22).

All eight rows are competitions, none is a phase: Primera Federacion's Grupo I/II and Segunda Federacion's groups are competition groups, not play-off stages, so E3G1/E3G2 and E4G2-E4G5 map 1:1 onto real groups by number.
Naming only: 'LaLiga2' is officially Segunda Division (branded LaLiga Hypermotion); 'LaLiga' is Primera Division / LaLiga EA Sports. Same competitions, no structural mismatch.

Out of our list but part of the pyramid: Segunda Federacion sends 27 clubs down to Tercera Federacion each season (25 direct - last five of each group - plus 2 from a play-off between the four worst 13th-placed teams); Tercera has no row here, so that outflow is unrepresentable.

Thailand.note: Thailand played spring-to-autumn until 2019; since 2020-21 the season is autumn/spring, so the current season is 2026-27.

Türkiye.real: not on the pyramid at all
Türkiye.note: U19 Süper Lig is the Süper Lig clubs' youth competition: entry is compulsory for the 18 senior clubs, fixtures mirror the senior list, no promotion or relegation. Keep it at level 99 and closed both ways; the field changes only when a senior club goes up or down.

Ukraine.real: no senior competition of that name exists
Ukraine.note: The Ukrainian pyramid is UPL - Persha Liha - Druha Liha. 'Premier Liga 2' matches the UPL's youth/reserve championship (U-21, 16 clubs, one per UPL club). Keep level 99 and closed; it must never promote or relegate.

Ukraine.real: 18 in the 2026-27 group list (9 + 9); the league infobox says 22
Ukraine.note: The infobox figure is stale. 18 is the correct count for 2026-27; note that group sizes flex every season with withdrawals.
Druha Liha clubs that finish last lose professional status and return to regional football, or simply withdraw; the PFL does not relegate them. Model exits, not relegations.

United States.real: two rival third-tier leagues in different organisations
United States.note: MLS Next Pro belongs to MLS (reserve/development clubs), USL League One to the USL. They never exchange clubs and there is no sporting link between them or to MLS/USL Championship.

Uruguay: UR2T is marked level 1; it is level 2 (Segunda División Profesional). This is the plain error the rows contain.

UR2T's label 'Torneo Competencia' names the opening phase (two series of 7 plus a final) of the second division, not a competition: the row's size 14 is the whole second division, so keeping it as a separate 'league' invents a 14-club competition that lasts six matchdays.
The two rows skip level 3. Segunda relegates 2 clubs per season into Primera Divisional C (28 clubs); with no level-3 row those clubs have nowhere to go and any move would shrink level 2.

The level-1 row does not encode that the season is three tournaments plus a semi-final/final; a simulator using one 16-club table for the whole year cannot reproduce the Apertura/Intermedio/Clausura reset or the champion play-off.
Relegation from level 1 depends on a two-season average table (Tabla de Descenso), not on the Clausura standings; nothing in the rows can hold that state.
No row records that 3 of the 14 second-division clubs are promoted each year (2 direct + 1 play-off), which is the only reason a 16-club and a 14-club league can exchange clubs every season.

Uzbekistan.note: 14 is correct for 2026 (the season article lists 14 clubs and 182 matches) but the league's own infobox and lead sentence still say 6. A row copied from last season would say 6 - and 14 clubs means 26 rounds, not 10.

Uzbekistan.note: The Pro League article describes bottom-club-down plus a 12th-v-3rd play-off; the 2026 Super League table instead marks 12th-15th as play-off places and 16th as direct relegation. Treat the 2026 markings as an unexplained one-off and implement the documented rule.

Uzbekistan.note: The regulations text says the last-placed club is relegated to the First League; the 2026 standings mark two places. Level 3 (First League) is not in our rows either way.

Venezuela.real: one 14-club competition played as two tournaments (Apertura, Clausura), each with a top-8 group phase and a final
Venezuela.note: The Clausura is the second half of the same league, not a separate division. Model two 13-round tournaments inside VZ1C, with the table resetting at mid-year and an aggregate table only for relegation.
The league article still says the two lowest are relegated; the last two seasons relegated exactly one (Yaracuyanos 2025, Anzoategui 2026). Use one.
